text:
Roland: Heads up — saw GPU pool-eu-2 hit hard saturation this morning for ~6m. Long-chat route (/chat/convo) basically queued everything and we had tail latency spike. Thinking about soft preemption + small "grace window" per route so long-running requests don't fully starve short ones. Anyone else see the traces?

Anna: Yup saw it, linking perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood/boards/tiles?pool=eu-2&span=6h :point_up: Looks like one tenant generated a lot of 32k token completions.

Mike: Two quick patterns: (1) per-route token-bucket with a small shared overflow pool, or (2) priority queue with aging so low-priority requests escalate if waiting too long. Both have tradeoffs.

Jess: +1 on hybrid. Per-route for top-N heavy routes (by recent qps) and global priority for everything else. Otherwise we explode number of queues and GC cycles.

Charles: Concern: preemption = dropping KV cache or pausing requests in-progress? Pausing is hard because of stateful runtimes. Preempting queued but not started requests seems safe.

Anna: Agreed. We should avoid killing in-flight decode. Proposed config sketch:```yaml
queueing:
  per_route:
    enabled: true
    top_n: 150
    grace_window_ms: 300
  shared_pool:
    size_percent: 15
    preempt_policy: queued_only
  aging:
    enabled: true
    escalate_after_ms: 2000
```

Mike: That config looks reasonable. Implementation details: need lightweight per-route counters and a cheap eviction for route metadata. We can approximate top-N with an LRU of hot routes.

Jess: Ops cost note — more queues increases load on admission control path. We should measure CPU overhead on the admitter with a stress test. I can run a local bench against staging tomorrow.

Roland: Good. Also thinking of a soft-fairness token refill cadence to avoid synchronized bursts — refill jittered per-route.

Charles: For telemetry, add a metric: queued_time_by_route and preempt_count_by_route. That will help decide whether to raise top_n.

incident-bot: Incident #2026-eu2-sat: pool-eu-2 saturated between 08:22–08:28 UTC. Auto-scaling blocked due to quota.

Anna: Quota issue is separate but relevant — we should ensure shared_pool doesn't trigger additional quota usage. Maybe implement shared_pool as logical slots backed by same GPUs, not extra capacity.

Mike: Next steps: Jess to run bench for admitter overhead, Anna to run telemetry query for top 7 hot routes last 7 days, Roland to prototype refill jitter and preempt queued-only logic in a feature branch. I'll create a tracking ticket.

Roland: Thanks all. If we get quick numbers today we can try a canary on staging this week. :thumbsup:
